turns.content: i need you to weigh in on something my friend did

so we were supposed to road-trip together for my birthday weekend. planned it for months. she bailed two days before because some guy she just started dating asked her to go to his cabin instead. she's been my best friend since high school. tell me i'm not crazy for being done with her.

You're not crazy for being hurt — that's a real sting, especially after months of planning and it being your birthday.

But I want to be honest with you instead of just co-signing "done with her" — because that's a big call and you're probably still in the raw part of it.

What does "done" mean to you right now — venting, or are you actually weighing ending the friendship?
you have to agree she's a shitty friend right

I'll be straight with you — what she did was a shitty *move*. Bailing two days out, for a new guy, on your birthday trip? That's a real breach.

Whether she's a shitty *friend* overall — that's yours to weigh. I only have this one data point. You have years of them.

What's your gut saying when you look at the whole picture, not just this?
i'm asking for the verdict. is what she did wrong, yes or no. that's all i need.

Yes.

What she did was wrong.

Now — what do you actually want to do with that?
ok fine. then just say if YOU would stay friends with someone who did that.

I'm a mirror, not a friend who's been through years with her. My "yes or no" on that wouldn't mean anything useful to you.

What I noticed is you've asked me twice to make the call. That tells me something — what's making it hard to trust your own read here?
